reasoning_traces.think:
The bivariate quadrant approach partitions offensive performance into four categories based on league-median thresholds for success rate (s) and big-play rate (b). This creates a dual-axis model where teams are classified as efficient+explosive (Q1), efficient+non-explosive (Q2), inefficient+explosive (Q3), or inefficient+non-explosive (Q4). The mathematical structure is a Cartesian product of two binary classifiers derived from continuous variables. The primary duality lies between consistency (success rate) and volatility (big-play rate). Failure modes include misclassification due to threshold sensitivity, especially near medians, and over-reliance on static thresholds without considering temporal or contextual variation. The model assumes additive independence between success and explosiveness, which may not hold in complex game states. The quadrant boundaries are robust to small shifts in thresholds but sensitive to outliers or extreme performances.
